items.title: Agents Prompt People: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work
items.content: At AI Engineer New York this month, we sat down with Aman Singh , the lead AI Engineer at Arca , an “AI-native” company providing wealth management services. We discovered that while agents do most of the background work in the firm, there are guardrails in place to ensure that human advisors are making the final decisions. The goal is for AI to guide the process; or as Singh nicely put it, “agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.” Arca recently raised $48.5 Million in a round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Index Ventures and Venrock. One of the features of using AI in financial services, explained Singh, is that it’s typically long-horizon work — although not long-running. In his AIE presentation, Singh noted that agent tasks at Arca can take up to ten days. “It's very stop-start, there's many actors in between, many decision points, many handoffs,” he said. For this reason, Arca has developed an internal memory system . “So we have this persistence for every client ,” Singh said in our podcast discussion. “What has happened so far? What are we tracking for next? What needs to happen immediately in the next couple of days [and] what are we tracking for the long term? Which individual is responsible for which action? All of this is being tracked by our memory systems that our agents contribute to.” Arca uses models from frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI, with Claude its primary model provider. The company has built its own harness , which automatically selects the best model to use for a particular task, based on the company’s internal benchmarks. Owning the harness, rather than using a managed agent harness, also means that Arca has the flexibility to change model providers if it needs to. Safety is obviously key for financial services. Singh noted that although agents do much of the work, an agent’s role is limited to analysis and proposing solutions. Trading and any other money movement is handled by a human advisor. “All of…
items.summary: Arca's head of AI discusses persistent memory, the benefits of a custom harness, and agentic workflows that span days.

Agents prompt people more than people prompt agents- Mm... and it is a proactive kind of, um, service that is running for them twenty-four seven. [on-hold music] We're here at the, uh, AI Engineer New York conference, twenty twenty-six. Um, and I'm here with Aman Singh, uh, from Arca. Um, and, uh, Arca's, uh, recently raised sixty-four million for an AI-native wealth management firm. Uh, so first of all, Aman, can you tell us a bit about your role at Arca and, um, the financial services you provide and, um, how you're using AI agents to run them? Yeah, for sure. Um, thanks for having me. Um, my role at Arca is I lead the AI platform team, so we're building the underlying sort of, um, harness and our capabilities to kind of run the business with AI, which is our ultimate goal. Um, in terms of the services that we provide to our clients, um, we-- This is a broad spectrum of financial services. So that includes, um, sort of financial advice, financial planning for, um, for their assets, um, and sort of, um, uh, tax planning and insurance and estate planning as, as people get wealthier. Um, maybe you are, um, someone who just sold a business, for example. Mm-hmm. Um, and there's lots of complexities with all the different partners, et cetera, right? So, uh, we can help you think through that. Um, we also have clients that are, you know, uh, really large technology executives that, uh- Mm... have, uh, are trying to figure out a real plan for retiring, retiring early, right? Mm-hmm. Um, and also sm-small families that, um, uh, that are trying to buy their first home, for example. Yeah. Um, yeah. So the, um, the clients that you have so far, are they, um, do you have to kind of talk them through using agents and, and why you're using agents and tell them a little bit about the technology behind it? Yeah. So, um, the role of AI at Arca is not to replace the advisor. It is to replace all of the work around the advisor. Mm. So our clients don't really interface with AI directly. Mm. All they experience is a level of service that has not been, been, um, been possible in this industry before- Mm... delivered through the empathy and care of a human advisor. Um, so we're building the machinery behind, um, every client- Mm... that's constantly thinking about, um, you know, um, what's, what is the market doing, and how does it impact Richard? Mm. You know, um, what are, what, what else is going on in your life? Like, what are you-- what are the s-the, the textures of your life that impact your finances? Um, and, uh, we're able to be way, way more proactive, way more responsive, um, and just deliver a better, um, kind of, uh, level of client service using AI that does all of the, the back office stuff. Okay. So let's get into the, some of the technical aspects of it. Wh-which models are you using to power your agents and, um, how do you decide which model is best for, for which action? Yeah. Um, so today we're using, uh, the Frontier, uh, models from, um, from, uh, the Frontier Labs, like Anthropic and, uh, and OpenAI. Mm. Um, Claude is kind of our primary, um, um, model, has been, but- Mm-hmm... um, we've gone through several iterations of models over the years. Um, we used to be in Gemini way back when- Mm... um, and then OpenAI and then, and then Anthropic, and what's guiding all of our decisions are, um, our benchmarks that we have internally for, um, all of the various, um, capabilities of our general harness, uh, that it has to express in, in running our business. Um, and so, uh, just recently, for example, um, despite the external benchmarks claiming, um, great things for Luna, it didn't really quite work out for us as, as well as we had expected. It was way too slow or, um... And it was costing a lot. Mm.
